cases.reason: The reader's CPL says 'no 1985 statement exposes a sequential record's number', but §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR4 (OK: "Comparisons for records in sequential files relate to the record number") and GR4d (OK: "the first existing record in the file whose record number is greater than the file position indicator is selected") make the sequential READ order depend on exactly this definition: record number is the ordinal number of the record in the file (§1985:III.2 p244, OK). A READ that returned records in any order other than their ordinal position violates p244 read with GR4, so a program's outcome depends on it, and the subject (the ordinal numbering of records in a file, which the implementation maintains) is not a property of the user's program. Not a derivation: it takes a witness; the probe above is a candidate own witness and the compiler is correct at 85.

DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 1.1 bars the definitional arm for a rule whose subject is the implementation. The row may fit informative (a vocabulary entry about the environment) but the definitional arm as named does not stand.

The identification is supplied by the message control system (the implementation) into an input CD's SYMBOLIC SOURCE; the originator is outside the user's program.
